newsitem.title: NORWAY: Rieber says buys Phoenix shares.
newsitem.headline: Rieber says buys Phoenix shares.

text.p: Norway's Rieber & Son, one of three bidders for Danish roadbuilder Phoenix, said on Tuesday that it had bought stock in the company during the past few days but gave no details of the amount involved.

"I can confirm that we have been buying shares in Phoenix Contractors in recent days but I cannot say how many. We intend to respect the rules of the game," Rieber managing director Olav Daviknes told Reuters.
Rieber last week announced that it held five percent of Phoenix shares but Daviknes would not say if its stake was now approaching the next statutory disclosure level of 10 percent.
Rieber & Son is currently the highest bidder for Phoenix, offering 725 crowns per A-share and 650 crowns each for the most-traded C-share.
The C-share had risen five Danish crowns on the Copenhagen market by midday Tuesday, up to 665 crowns from Monday's closing 660.
The other bidders are Danish construction and chemicals group Superfos A/S and small provincial Danish building contractor Marius Pedersen.
Phoenix has called shareholders to an extraordinary meeting on February 21, prior to making its final recommendation. -Terje Solsvik, Oslo newsroom +47-22936975
